Notes: This table reports heterogeneous effects for the primary outcome of per capita daily consumption with respect to baseline covariates identified using the generalized random forest method. context_needed: Somalia (Baidoa), Ultra-Poor Graduation (UPG) programme for displaced households; Leight, Hirvonen, Karachiwalla and Rakshit (IFPRI DP 02356, 2025). Household-level RCT; UPG = assignment to the programme (ITT); specification (PDF p. 13) adds strata fixed effects and the baseline outcome where measured. Outcome: household per capita daily consumption in 2017 PPP dollars (PDF p. 12). N = 3,964 matches the consumption column of Table 2 (PDF p. 30), i.e. the second follow-up, 28 months after baseline (PDF p. 11). Interpretation (PDF p. 22): the subgroup dummies equal one for households below the 25th percentile at baseline, so the UPG coefficient is the effect for the omitted group (households of 5 or more members; dependency ratio 2.5 or above; baseline assets not low), and each UPG X term is how much larger the effect is in the flagged group. In column (4) the UPG coefficient is the effect for households in the omitted group on all three dimensions at once.

rule: In a treatment x subgroup regression, the treatment coefficient is the effect for the omitted subgroup (stored with that subgroup named), the interaction is the difference in effect between the two subgroups (stored as such, never as an effect for the flagged group), and the subgroup dummy is a covariate (not stored). With several interactions in one column, the omitted group is the one that is omitted on every dimension.

resolved_questions.question: The interaction terms are stored here as 'difference in effect between subgroups', following the instruction for this pattern, but the stored-rows rules only name 'change in effect between rounds'. Confirm the effect_type name, and whether the summed effect for the flagged subgroup (not printed) should ever be derived.
resolved_questions.resolution: Reviewer convention, 22 Nov 2026: 'difference in effect between subgroups' is the effect_type for interaction terms. The summed effect for the flagged subgroup is never computed by the reader.
